Simple Present Passive Questions

The passive voice is used when the doer of an action is not necessary, is understood or is unknown. This voice is used in the simple present tense to talk about processes and actions that take place on a regular basis.

Now, we’re going to learn how to ask questions using the simple present tense in the passive voice.
Now, are human resources included in a computer-based information system?
Are they considered an important part of this system?

Remember that the passive form in any tense is always made of the verb to be and the past participle form of the main verb.

The verb to be usually goes in the tense we want to use; for our particular case this verb should go in its simple present tense form (am, is, are) and it is followed by the main verb in its past participle form. For the interrogative form, all you have to do is place the verb to be before the subject, as shown in the chart below:

Negative Questions to Express an Opinion
Negative Questions can be used as a conversation strategy.
Don't you think it is time to review some of the concepts to be ready?
Don't you think we can get started instead of waiting for the manager to back us up?

Negative Questions is a helpful conversation strategy that will help you state opinions in a polite way, and also to suggest agreement with what you say.

Look at the following examples:

  • Don’t you think we can finish this project today?
  • Shouldn’t we start planning our board meeting?
  • Haven’t you thought about checking this software out? It is really good.
  • Why don’t we start the meeting now, it’s getting late?

These are not real questions, but they are asking the listener to agree with what they state.
Shouldn't we talk about it?
Don't you think we're more than ready to give that training?
Difference Between Computers and Information Systems
The fields of computer science and information systems have some differences; the section below explains their main characteristics.

Computers are effective and efficient ways to process data, and engineers and software developers consider them a necessary part of an information system. However, it is also said that an Information System (IS), involves much more than just computers.

Ryan: Hey, Alice. The training on IS starts next Wednesday. Don't you think it is time to review some of the concepts to be ready?
Alice: Sure. But, why don't we talk to the manager? He always arranges a meeting with some of the experts to give us some guidelines.
Ryan: Don't you think we can get started instead of waiting for the manager to back us up? He's always complaining about how we cannot do things on our own.
Alice: You're right. Let's do it! We can't forget that we need to learn a lot about data in computer-based information systems ASAP so we can train ourselves the rest of the team.
Ryan: Exactly! That's why I'm worried. Let's start by getting some questions ready. The first one and most important is about computer-based information system. What is it?

Alice: That's an easy one. A computer-based information system is a type of system that uses computer technology to undergo some or all of its intended tasks. The simplest form of this system can be represented in a personal computer and software.
Ryan: Well answered. Now, are human resources included in a computer-based information system?
Alice: Yes, they are. On the one hand, we have the people in charge of making things work; for instance, IS specialists, system analysts, programmers and data administrators. On the other hand, we have the end users, which are the clients or users.
Ryan: What about data resources? Are they considered an important part of this system? Shouldn't we talk about it?

Alice: Of course, we should. Data resources include data and databases. Data is considered the raw material of information systems and can take many forms: the usual alphanumeric data, text data, image data, and audio data. Now, I have a question for you, Ryan. Are data resources required to meet any criteria?
Ryan: Yes, of course. They must be comprehensive, which means all the data regarding a particular subject is actually present in the database. There shouldn't be any redundancy, and data should be stored to minimize the cost of expected processing and storage as much as possible. One last question Alice, how are data resources of IS organized?
Alice: Well, they're organized into processed and organized data-databases and into knowledge in many forms, which can be facts, rules, and case examples related to successful business practices.
Ryan: Don't you think we're more than ready to give that training?
Alice: The manager is going to be so proud of us!
